title: Generation of transgene-free human induced pluripotent stem cells from erythroblasts
author: Perriot, Canales, et al.

steps.title: Collect blood in EDTA tubes
steps.instruction: Draw 10 mL of peripheral blood from the donor into an EDTA‑coated tube; donors aged 2–55 years are acceptable and the redder colour of children’s erythroblasts does not affect reprogramming efficiency.

steps.title: Set incubator to 37 °C, 5% CO₂
steps.instruction: Verify that the humidified incubator is set to 37 °C and 5 % CO₂ for culturing human erythroblasts, hiPSCs and differentiated cells.

steps.title: Prepare and store culture media
steps.instruction: Prepare erythroblast medium, ReproTeSR, and StemMACS human iPSC Brew according to the manufacturers’ recipes; store erythroblast medium at 4 °C for up to 1 week and the iPSC media at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks; bring all media to room temperature or 37 °C before adding to cells.

steps.title: Schedule start on Thursday
steps.instruction: Plan to begin the reprogramming workflow on a Thursday to minimise cell handling over the weekend.

substeps.instruction: Pour 10 mL of Ficoll‑Paque PLUS into a 50 mL Falcon tube.

In a second 50 mL Falcon tube, combine the 10 mL of freshly drawn blood with 10 mL of PBS; mix gently (homogenise). If processing is delayed, keep the blood at room temperature on a rocker for no more than 8 h.
Carefully layer the diluted blood over the Ficoll without mixing.
Centrifuge at 750 g for 20 min at room temperature with the brake off.
Using a 10 mL pipette, aspirate as much plasma (upper yellow layer) as possible, leaving the whitish PBMC ring at the plasma‑Ficoll interface undisturbed.
Transfer the PBMC ring to a new 50 mL Falcon tube; add 30 mL RPMI; centrifuge at 550 g for 10 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant; resuspend the pellet in 10 mL RPMI; count the cells; centrifuge at 750 g for 10 min at room temperature.

Discard the supernatant; resuspend cells in freezing solution of FBS/DMSO (90:10) at 10 × 10⁶ cells/mL; aliquot 5–10 × 10⁶ cells per cryotube; place tubes at –80 °C. After 3 days, transfer to liquid nitrogen for long‑term storage.

description: The execution of this protocol requires prior blood draw and standard peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) isolation. Only 10 mL of blood collected in EDTA tubes is required. This protocol is suitable for the reprogramming of erythroblasts from both adults and children (protocol tested in our hands on donors from 2 to 55 year-old without any difference in efficiency. The only difference observed is that erythroblasts from children are redder than from adults but this does not affect the efficiency of reprogramming). Human erythroblasts, hiPSCs and differentiated cells were all cultured in a humidified 37°C incubator and 5% CO2. Prior to beginning the reprogramming protocol, prepare media, solutions, and matrix-coated culture dishes. Once prepared, erythroblast medium can be kept at 4°C for 1 week while ReproTeSR and StemMACS human iPSC Brew media can be kept at 4°C for 2 weeks. All media should be brought to room temperature or 37°C prior to adding on the cells. This protocol is optimized to be started on a Thursday to minimize cell handling during the weekends.
